page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6r.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance based on the 64-bit ARM architecture. Powered by a 2.8 GHz Ampere Altra processor managed via the KVM hypervisor, the instance provides 16 dedicated physical-equivalent vCPUs paired with 32.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:2 compute-to-memory allocation ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware, relying on external network-attached block storage and operating with a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile.

Benchmark measurements reflect the architectural characteristics of the Ampere Altra core. In multi-threaded testing, the instance achieves solid middle-tier throughput, demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 28,612.3, a Geekbench multi-core rating of 9,534.0, and 22.17 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. Large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 135.55 GB/s with write throughput reaching 69.0 GB/s. Static web serving throughput registers at 18.56 GB/s, and software compilation via Clang produces a stable Geekbench subscore of 17,034.0.

In contrast, single-thread compute metrics display predictable lower-tier performance typical of first-generation ARM enterprise cores running at modest clock frequencies. Geekbench single-core performance scores at 1,104.0, single-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 8.6 GB/s, and PassMark CPU encryption scores at 2,558.55, placing them in the lower quartile of comparative benchmarks. Furthermore, medium-sized language model prompt processing rates (19.07 tokens/sec for 7B models) highlight limitations when handling demanding vectorized floating-point calculations.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, ecs.c6r.4xlarge offers density and compute efficiency for horizontally scaled Linux workloads compiled for AArch64. The absence of integrated storage necessitates remote volumes for persistent state, but the steady multi-core execution makes it well suited for distributed microservices, static web servers, multi-threaded batch processors, containerized CI/CD workers, and scalable Redis caches.
